A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Depth Pro, with matching authors, core methods and experiments. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original depth, boundary-accuracy and focal-length results in Tables 1–3, together with runtime measurements, controlled experiments and qualitative applications in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds resolution and depth-representation experiments, plus boundary scores for existing training ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the multi-scale ViT/DPT architecture, canonical inverse-depth objectives, two-stage curriculum and separately trained focal-length branch. The revised Figure 3 and new implementation subsections provide fuller specifications of existing components; they do not establish a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is retained. UnrealStereo4K, used in the new resolution study, already appears in v1's boundary experiments; Hypersim already supports training and evaluation. The added studies vary resolution, prediction targets and evaluation depth ranges within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The benchmark and backbone comparator sets are unchanged. The four focal-length variants in v1 Table 12 are renamed in v2 Table 14 with identical scores. Method names in new Table 7 illustrate output resolutions; that table evaluates resampled ground truth, not additional baseline models.

E3.justification: Added supplementary protocols compare four ground-truth resampling resolutions and train ViT/DPT predictors on Hypersim with three depth representations, evaluating six distance ranges. Existing training ablations gain boundary F1 evaluation. Previously documented training budgets, dataset splits, sample counts and principal evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Controlled validation expands substantially: v2 adds a native-resolution comparison beyond v1's perturbation study, introduces an inverse-depth/log-depth/direct-depth ablation, and adds boundary measurements to stage-1, stage-2 and full-curriculum comparisons. Tables 7 and 10–13 directly investigate several central design choices behind sharp predictions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests for performance estimates. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial controlled results are added while previously reported scores remain unchanged. v2 Table 7 reports resampled-ground-truth F1 of 0.044 at 384×384 and 0.311 at 1536×1536. Table 10 reports 0–1 m accuracy of 0.730, 0.700 and 0.657 for inverse, log and direct depth. Tables 11–13 add boundary scores, including curriculum F1 of 0.465 versus single-stage training's 0.478.

T1.justification: The loss equations, boundary definitions and precision/recall formulation are unchanged, including Equations 1–3. No theorem, proof or mathematical derivation is added. The resolution upper-bound discussion and Voronoi merging description are empirical interpretation and implementation detail, respectively.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit contribution claim that high native resolution is necessary but insufficient for accurate boundaries. The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims about fast, sharp, zero-shot metric depth and focal-length estimation.

C2.justification: v2 interprets real-data diversity as potentially outweighing noisy gradient supervision and explicitly acknowledges the curriculum's metric-depth versus boundary-accuracy tradeoff. It qualifies the resolution experiment as an upper-bound analysis. Existing limitations concerning translucent surfaces and volumetric scattering remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Sections C.1–C.2 specify Voronoi-based patch merging and the focal head's convolution kernels, strides and channels. Figure 3 adds tensor dimensions and feature-fusion detail. Training hyperparameters, access information and the previously documented 35-patch, 25% overlap configuration are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and substantive research positioning are retained. References for DepthFM, Metric3D v2 and Depth Anything v2 receive publication updates, alongside bibliographic corrections, without introducing new related works.

P1.justification: Local rewrites clarify the network, training interpretations and focal-length variants. New appendix subsections and more specific cross-references improve navigation, and the header changes to ICLR 2025 publication status. The overall organization and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 3, adds the merge illustration in Figure 11 and two experimental tables, and adds F1 columns to three existing ablation tables. The focal-length table expands, several displays move, and captions are refined. Most empirical figures and the overall visual format remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds direct boundary evidence to training ablations that previously reported only depth-accuracy metrics, supports resolution and representation choices with controlled studies, and documents merging and focal-head implementation. Explicitly acknowledging the curriculum's lower boundary F1 improves interpretation. These provide bounded gains in evidential support and reproducibility while the main method and headline comparative results remain unchanged.
